datos.forma_craneo: mesocéfalo. frente ligeramente abovedada, no muy ancha; protuberancia occipital perceptible.
datos.orejas: De tamaño mediano, implantación relativamente alta para un sabueso francés, planas y ligeramente giradas hacia adentro en la parte inferior.
datos.recomendaciones_higiene: cepillado regular para eliminar pelo muerto y mantener el pelaje saludable. limpieza de oidos y corte de unas segun sea necesario.
datos.alimentacion_recomendada: dieta equilibrada de alta calidad, formulada para perros activos de tamano grande. ajustar la cantidad segun nivel de actividad y metabolismo.
datos.recomendaciones_alimentacion: evitar la sobrealimentacion para prevenir la obesidad. monitorizar el peso y la condicion corporal.
datos.recomendaciones_ejercicio_diario: Paseos largos y vigorosos, oportunidades para correr en áreas seguras, juegos de olfato.
datos.advertencias_sobreesfuerzo: Evitar ejercicio extenuante en climas muy calurosos o en cachorros en crecimiento.
datos.entorno_ideal: Espacio amplio al aire libre, campo o finca.
datos.recomendaciones_adaptacion: Requiere un dueño experimentado que pueda manejar su energía y su instinto de caza. La socialización temprana es crucial.
datos.cuidados_emocionales_recomendados: Proporcionar compañía y actividad. Evitar periodos prolongados de soledad.
datos.recomendaciones_generales_bienestar: Mantener su mente y cuerpo activos. Proporcionar un ambiente seguro y estimulante.
datos.uso_original: Sabueso utilizado para la caza mayor, especialmente de jabalí y ciervo, gracias a su resistencia y olfato.
datos.uso_actual: Principalmente como perro de caza, pero también como compañero para personas activas que disfrutan del aire libre.
datos.riesgos_craneo: Riesgos moderados: otitis, problemas dentales y riesgos propios de cada raza.

estandar.texto: FEDERATION CYNOLOGIQUE INTERNATIONALE (AISBL) SECRETARIAT GENERAL: 13, Place Albert 1er B – 6530 Thuin (Belgique) ______________________________________________________________________________ _______________________________________________________________ _______________________________________________________________ 24.04.1997/EN FCI-Standard N° 25 BILLY 2 TRANSLATION: Mrs. Kincaid, brought up to date by Dr. Paschoud. Official language (FR). ORIGIN: France. DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 28.12.1973. UTILIZATION: Hound. FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 6 Scenthounds and related breeds. Section 1.1 Large sized hounds. With working trial. GENERAL APPEARANCE: Well constructed hound, strong, yet light; forequarters more powerful than hindquarters. HEAD: Fairly fine, lean, of medium length. CRANIAL REGION: Skull: Forehead slightly domed, not very broad; occipital protuberance perceptible. Stop: Well defined. FACIAL REGION: Nose: Well developed, black or red-brown. Muzzle: Rather square. Nasal bridge fairly broad; first straight, then slightly arched, moderately long. Lips: Slightly or not at all in form of flews, the upper lip covering the lower without overhanging fleshiness; corner of the lips often visible. EYES: Alert, very open and dark, eye rims black or brown. EARS: Leathers of medium size, set on relatively high for a French hound, rather flat, in the lower section turning slightly inwards. 3 NECK Of medium length, rather round, somewhat strong; a slight dewlap is permitted. BODY: Back: Rather wide, strong, slightly arched. Loin: Wide, slightly arched. Croup: Sloping. Chest: Very deep, quite narrow. Ribs: Flat. Underline and belly: Flank fairly long, with a slight tuck-up. TAIL: Long, strong, sometimes slightly feathered. LIMBS FOREQUARTERS: General appearance: Strong, vertical stance, flat bones. Shoulder: Fairly long, lying close to the chest. Forefeet: Well developed, rather round; toes tight. HINDQUARTERS: Thighs: Moderately muscled. Hocks: Slightly bent, wide and strong. Hind feet: Well developed, rather round; toes tight. GAIT/MOVEMENT: Gallops easily. SKIN: White, sometimes with deep brown or almost black spots; supple and fine. COAT Hair: Short, harsh to the touch, often slightly coarse. Colour: Pure white or milk-coffee white, or white with light orange or lemon patches or mantle. SIZE: For dogs : 60-70 cm. For bitches : 58-62 cm. 4 FAULTS : Any departure from the foregoing points should be considered a fault and the seriousness with which the fault should be regarded should be in exact proportion to its degree and its effect upon the health and welfare of the dog. DISQUALIFYING FAULTS: • Aggressive or overly shy. • Any dog clearly showing physical or behavioural abnormalities. • Nasal bridge too short, too long or too slim. • Pronounced overshot mouth; such a dog must be stristly disqualified; however a dog with a slightly overshot mouth (1/2 cm) has not to be eliminated. • Black or red hair. N.B.: • Male animals should have two apparently normal testicles fully descended into the scrotum. • Only functionally and clinically healthy dogs, with breed typical conformation should be used for breeding.
